verses.text: “Woe to the rebellious children”, says Yahweh, “who take counsel, but not from me; and who make an alliance, but not with my Spirit, that they may add sin to sin,
who set out to go down into Egypt, and have not asked my advice; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to take refuge in the shadow of Egypt!
Therefore the strength of Pharaoh will be your shame, and the refuge in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.
For their princes are at Zoan, and their ambassadors have come to Hanes.
They shall all be ashamed because of a people that can’t profit them, that are not a help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach.”

The burden of the animals of the South. Through the land of trouble and anguish, of the lioness and the lion, the viper and fiery flying serpent, they carry their riches on the shoulders of young donkeys, and their treasures on the humps of camels, to an unprofitable people.
For Egypt helps in vain, and to no purpose; therefore I have called her Rahab who sits still.
Now go, write it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for the time to come forever and ever.
For it is a rebellious people, lying children, children who will not hear Yahweh’s law;
who tell the seers, “Don’t see!” and to the prophets, “Don’t prophesy to us right things. Tell us pleasant things. Prophesy deceits.
Get out of the way. Turn aside from the path. Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.”
Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel, “Because you despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and rely on it;
therefore this iniquity shall be to you like a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking comes suddenly in an instant.

He will break it as a potter’s vessel is broken, breaking it in pieces without sparing, so that there won’t be found among the broken piece a piece good enough to take fire from the hearth, or to dip up water out of the cistern.”
For thus said the Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,
but you said, “No, for we will flee on horses”; therefore you will flee; and, “We will ride on the swift”; therefore those who pursue you will be swift.
One thousand will flee at the threat of one. At the threat of five, you will flee until you are left like a beacon on the top of a mountain, and like a banner on a hill.
Therefore Yahweh will wait, that he may be gracious to you; and therefore he will be exalted, that he may have mercy on you, for Yahweh is a God of justice. Blessed are all those who wait for him.
For the people will dwell in Zion at Jerusalem. You will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the voice of your cry. When he hears you, he will answer you.
Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teachers won’t be hidden any more, but your eyes will see your teachers;
and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
You shall defile the overlaying of your engraved images of silver, and the plating of your molten images of gold. You shall cast them away as an unclean thing. You shall tell it, “Go away!”
He will give the rain for your seed, with which you will sow the ground; and bread of the increase of the ground will be rich and plentiful. In that day, your livestock will feed in large pastures.
The oxen likewise and the young donkeys that till the ground will eat savory feed, which has been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.
There shall be brooks and streams of water on every lofty mountain and on every high hill in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

Moreover the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, in the day that Yahweh binds up the fracture of his people, and heals the wound they were struck with.
Behold, Yahweh’s name comes from far away, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a devouring fire.
His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction; and a bridle that leads to ruin will be in the jaws of the peoples.
You will have a song, as in the night when a holy feast is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come to Yahweh’s mountain, to Israel’s Rock.
Yahweh will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.
For through Yahweh’s voice the Assyrian will be dismayed. He will strike him with his rod.
Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which Yahweh will lay on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.
For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.

footnotes.content: Here's a hard word: the children rebelling don't even ask God's counsel before they make their big moves. They just decide and go. How much of my own striving comes from not stopping to ask the Lord first? He's already here, waiting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Egypt—the ancient superpower, the place of refuge when Israel was small. But the Lord's saying: you don't need Pharaoh's strength when I'm beside you. We still reach for Egypt sometimes: worldly power that looks strong and leaves us empty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The shame comes not from trusting God and losing, but from trusting power that was never strong enough to begin with. A good reminder: false refuges always fail. Only the Lord stands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zoan and Hanes—real cities in Egypt where the ambassadors go to make their deals. The prophet names the specific places where Israel grasps for human help instead of calling out to God. Names matter: they show us where we're really turning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A people that can't profit them. This hits hard. We spend so much effort on relationships, alliances, pursuits that promise but deliver shame. The question isn't whether to trust someone—it's whether they're actually worth your trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Picture the caravan straining through dangerous land—lions, vipers, scorching heat—burdened down with treasure they're carrying to Egypt. All that danger and effort for people who won't even help. I see the futility now, and it breaks my heart for them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rahab means pride or arrogance—what a name for a false refuge! Egypt sits still, helpless to truly save. When we name what we're really relying on, its weakness becomes plain. The Lord calls us to see it: this trust is hollow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Write it down, inscribe it—make it permanent. God's not just speaking in anger; He's preserving this word so generations will know: this is what happens when we turn away. His warnings are mercies, written so we can learn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rebellious, lying children who won't hear—that's not a description of them alone. How often do I plug my ears to what I don't want to hear? The refusal to listen is what traps us in our own small world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tell us pleasant things; prophesy deceits. Oh, how we still want this. We want the sermon that feels good, the truth that costs us nothing. But a prophet who lies isn't being kind—he's leading us over a cliff.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Get the Holy One of Israel out of our way. That's the root of it, isn't it? Not ignorance—a deliberate pushing aside. They knew God was there; they just didn't want Him in the room while they made their plans.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Because you despise this word—God ties their judgment directly to their refusal to listen. When we reject His counsel, we're choosing the consequences that follow. He doesn't hide the road; we turn away from it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A breach in a high wall that suddenly collapses—the judgment comes swift and irreversible. What they trusted to hold them up crumbles in an instant. This is what happens when we build on the wrong foundation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Broken like a potter's vessel without pity—not a single usable piece left. The completeness of it is terrible. And yet: even in judgment, the Lord is still the Potter. He could reshape them if they'd turn and let Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In returning and rest you'll be saved; in quietness and confidence is your strength. These are the paths the Lord set before them, and they said no. What am I refusing that looks like rest and trust? He's already offering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We'll flee on horses; we'll ride on the swift—their answer to God's offer is to trust their own speed, their own escape. But you can't outrun judgment you brought on yourself. Pride chooses flight over rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A thousand fleeing at the threat of one—terror so complete that tiny pressure breaks them. When we've turned away from God's strength, even small enemies loom like mountains. We become fragile in our pride.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh will wait, that he may be gracious—even in judgment, His heart is turned toward mercy. The Lord delays to give room for repentance. Blessed are all those who wait for Him—this is the invitation still standing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You will weep no more—the promise turns. When Israel returns to Zion, when tears cease, it's because the Lord Himself answers the cry of His people. This is the arc: judgment, then grace. The cry gets answered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Though the Lord gives bread of adversity—comfort doesn't mean ease. In hardship, your teachers won't be hidden; they'll be visible, real. The Lord doesn't remove all difficulty; He gives us wisdom and guides within it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A voice behind you saying, This is the way—not a distant instruction, but intimate guidance for each turn. When we finally stop fleeing and listen, His direction is right there: practical, personal, always near.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You shall defile your engraved images, cast them away—the turning includes putting away false gods. Repentance isn't just feeling sorry; it's a decisive act of throwing down what we trusted instead of Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will give the rain for your seed; bread of the increase will be rich and plentiful—the Lord restores abundance, not scarcity. This isn't earned; it's the gift He gives when His people turn back to Him and obey.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The oxen and young donkeys will eat savory feed—even the animals taste the blessing when God's people return to Him. There's a wholeness to restoration: it touches the earth itself, the livestock, all the Lord has made.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Brooks and streams on every lofty mountain in the day of great slaughter—when God defeats the enemies, He waters the high places. What was barren blooms. This is the reversal the faithful await.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The light of the moon like the sun's light, the sun seven times brighter—a day of overwhelming brilliance. When the Lord heals the wounds of His people, darkness flees completely. Everything is remade in His light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Behold, Yahweh's name comes from far away, burning with his anger—the Lord's judgment is not arbitrary or petty. His anger is holiness encountering what mars His creation. It's the wrath of love itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His breath as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations—the Lord's power judges with precision. A bridle in the jaws of peoples speaks of control: He restrains the chaos nations make.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You will have a song, as in the night when a holy feast is kept, with gladness of heart—the joy of the redeemed is real and full. Walking toward Yahweh's mountain, toward the Rock of Israel: this is what Israel sings about.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh will cause his glorious voice to be heard, will show the descent of his arm—the Lord doesn't work in secret. His mighty acts are visible, audible; the nations will see Him at work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Through Yahweh's voice the Assyrian will be dismayed—the specific enemy (Assyria was the superpower of the day) falls at God's word alone. He won't need Israel's weapons or alliances. The Lord's voice does what swords cannot.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every stroke of the rod, with the sound of tambourines and harps—even judgment becomes worship. The Lord's justice is so complete that Israel celebrates it with joy. His victory is their deliverance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this final word: the burning place prepared, the king's pyre ready, Yahweh's breath kindling fire. We see Christ's victory over all powers of death and darkness, the enemy's defeat already written before time began. As of 2026-10, we live in that triumph.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
